# Base egress allowlist, installed as
# /etc/devcontainer/firewall-allowlist.d/00-base.txt.
#
# Applied only when DEVCONTAINER_FIREWALL=on. One entry per line:
#
#   example.com       a domain; every A record it resolves to is allowed
#   140.82.112.0/20   a CIDR block, used as-is
#   169.254.1.2       a bare address
#   +github-meta      expand GitHub's published ranges from api.github.com/meta
#
# Do not edit this file to add project-specific hosts. Drop another .txt into the
# same directory instead (numbered above 00 so the ordering reads sensibly), which
# keeps your additions from being lost when the image is rebuilt:
#
#   RUN echo 'my-internal-registry.example.com' \
#       > /etc/devcontainer/firewall-allowlist.d/50-project.txt

# --- Claude Code: inference, auth, telemetry -------------------------------
api.anthropic.com
console.anthropic.com
claude.ai
sentry.io
# statsig.anthropic.com is deliberately absent: it has neither an A nor an AAAA
# record, so listing it only produced a resolution warning on every start. Set
# CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1 in containerEnv to turn telemetry and
# error reporting off rather than allowlisting sentry.io above.

# --- GitHub ----------------------------------------------------------------
# The named hosts sit behind large rotating pools, so resolved A records go stale
# within minutes; +github-meta adds the published ranges that actually back them.
# Also covers release tarballs, which is how `uv python install` fetches
# interpreters (python-build-standalone) and how yq/rga were installed at build.
+github-meta
github.com
api.github.com
codeload.github.com
objects.githubusercontent.com
raw.githubusercontent.com

# --- GitHub Copilot CLI ----------------------------------------------------
# Inference, auth and the CLI's own login exchange. Like the GitHub hosts above it
# sits behind a rotating pool, so the +github-meta expansion above is what actually
# keeps it reachable -- it now includes the published `copilot` ranges, which are
# Azure addresses that appear under no other key.
api.githubcopilot.com
# default.exp-tas.com, the CLI's feature-flag endpoint, is deliberately absent even
# though GitHub publishes it as a Copilot domain: it is a CNAME into e-msedge.net,
# whose address (13.107.5.93) is already one of those `copilot` ranges. Listing the
# name on top of that only helps if the resolver answers it at all -- one that
# blackholes e-msedge.net returns 0.0.0.0, and allowlisting 0.0.0.0 is worse than
# listing nothing.

# --- Python ----------------------------------------------------------------
pypi.org
files.pythonhosted.org
astral.sh

# --- Node ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Claude Code auto-updates itself from here.
registry.npmjs.org

# --- Ubuntu ----------------------------------------------------------------
archive.ubuntu.com
security.ubuntu.com
ports.ubuntu.com
esm.ubuntu.com

# --- Container registries --------------------------------------------------
# The image ships rootless podman, so a `podman pull` or a `FROM` in a
# `podman build` has to resolve somewhere. Registries need two hosts, not one:
# the API host issues the manifest and a separate CDN host serves the blobs, and
# a pull that reaches only the first fails halfway through with a signed URL in
# the error message. Docker Hub uses two CDNs and hands out either.
#
# This is also where the allowlist is at its most fragile: those CDN names sit
# behind rotating pools, resolved once at container start, so a long-running
# container can find that a pull which worked an hour ago no longer does.
# Restarting it re-resolves everything.
registry-1.docker.io
auth.docker.io
index.docker.io
production.cloudflare.docker.com
production.cloudfront.docker.com
# ghcr.io serves its blobs from pkg-containers.githubusercontent.com, which is
# not covered by the +github-meta ranges above.
ghcr.io
pkg-containers.githubusercontent.com
quay.io
cdn.quay.io
cdn01.quay.io
cdn02.quay.io
cdn03.quay.io
# Where the devcontainer base images live, so this repo's own image can be built
# inside a container of itself.
mcr.microsoft.com

# --- apt sources added by the language images -------------------------------
# The python image installs Google Chrome, which leaves an apt source behind; without
# this, `apt-get update` inside a firewalled container fails on it confusingly.
dl.google.com
